the economic effect of GDP per capita is the main driving force for CO2 emissions in the ASEAN and China.

China and the ASEANS are facing tremendous challenges in terms of the balance between economic development and low carbon development, and that the economic effect of per capita GDP has a significant impact on the increase of CO2 emissions.
economic effect in terms per capita GDP is dominant in the total CO2 emissions in the ASEAN region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the decomposition of CO2 emissions and decoupling of economic growth from CO2 emissions in the context of ASEAN countries.
the decomposition of carbon emissions and the relationship between economic development and carbon emissions in China and the Association for Southeast Asian Nations ( ASEAN ).

the relationship between economic development and CO2 emissions in China and the 10 ASEAN countries, which are Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economic effect is the most important driving force for the growth of CO2 emissions in China and ASEAN countries.
the ASEAN region as a whole has not yet reached the stage of decoupling CO2 emissions from economic growth.
the decoupling of economic growth from environmental pressures is possible in China and the majority of ASEAN countries, but the decoupling effect has not been achieved yet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in China and the Association for Southeast Asian Nations ( ASEAN) countries, carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions have a strong correlation with economic growth and energy consumption, and energy intensity has played an important role in reducing carbon dioxide emissions in most of these countries.
China and ASEAN have to be more concerned about the environmental issues, and should make efforts to decouple economic growth and carbon dioxide emissions.
China and the ASEAn countries should take measures to promote the use of renewable energy, improve energy efficiency and reduce energy intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
China and the ASE AN need to decouple economic growth and CO2 emissions in a coordinated way.
energy efficiency improvement is a crucial factor to achieve decoupling between economic growth and CO2 emissions.
energy policies in China need to be scaled up to decouple economic growth and environmental pressure in the ASEAN region.
